Where Culture Fades: Revealing the Cultural Gap in Text-to-Image Generation

A model may contain cultural knowledge yet fail to activate it when generating images from multilingual prompts.

Shi Chuancheng · Li Shangze · Guo Shiming · Xie Simiao · Wu Wenhua · Dou Jingtong · Wu Chao · Xiao Canran · Wang Cong · Cheng Zifeng · Shen Fei · Chua Tat-Seng

November 21, 2025 ·CVPR 2026 · Highlight ·Read the paper ·PDF
1Why this matters 2How it works 3What the study finds 4What this means

The short version

Where Culture Fades investigates under-activation of cultural representations in text-to-image models. It traces where cultural information weakens, identifies sparse culture-related neurons, and tests inference-time activation and targeted enhancement. CultureBench connects these internal analyses to the cultural fidelity of generated images.

The study distinguishes possessing a representation from successfully expressing it. It examines whether changing the activation of existing knowledge can improve culture-specific generation while tracking generation quality and diversity.

2Representative models analyzed
SparseCulture-sensitive neurons
2Complementary alignment strategies

Cultural knowledge can be present in a model yet fail to shape what it generates.

Why this matters

Visual realism and semantic alignment do not ensure that images preserve the cultural connotations of a prompt across languages.

How it works

  1. Analyze cultural consistency under multilingual prompts in representative text-to-image models.
  2. Probe a small set of culture-sensitive neurons concentrated in selected layers.
  3. Amplify selected neurons at inference time or update only culturally relevant layers.

What the study finds

Analyses of two representative models support under-activation rather than simply missing knowledge. CultureBench evaluations report improved cultural consistency while preserving fidelity and diversity.

What this means

This distinction matters whenever a model’s output is used to judge the scope of its knowledge. A generic image may reflect weak access to cultural detail, incomplete knowledge, or both. Internal analysis makes those explanations more separable and enables a more specific intervention.

The broader goal is culturally faithful generation grounded in identifiable mechanisms and measured outcomes. The reported findings establish a direction within the tested models and cultural coverage, while richer local evaluation remains essential for understanding what fidelity means across communities.
